evidence_reviewed: ES query: clearflow-*,clearflow-healthmonitor-* range covering the injection window
Health witness log: zero DOWN events across all 8 services for the entire window -- redis outage produced no health-check-visible symptom on any service
Direct event-type funnel count: 14 PAYMENT_SUBMITTED, 12 PAYMENT_VALIDATED, 11 PAYMENT_ROUTED, 11 SETTLEMENT_COMPLETE -- essentially normal end-to-end throughput, no stall
Searched all events for redis-related messages, ERROR-level log lines, or unusual rejection patterns -- found only 2 ordinary EMBARGOED_COUNTRY business rejections, unrelated to redis
reasoning_trace: This is the first live test of the newly-built REDIS_OUTAGE mechanism (real docker stop/start on the shared redis container, confirmed via docker ps -a during the run: Exited(0) then Up/healthy). Unlike every crash-based fault in this catalog, a 20-second redis outage produced literally no detectable evidence anywhere: no health-check failure on any of the 8 services (none apparently treat redis connectivity as a hard dependency for their own /actuator/health), no funnel stall (payments flowed through essentially normally), no redis-related error messages. This is a genuine, honest null result, not a mechanism failure -- the fault definitely ran for real (confirmed via direct docker inspection during the window), it just produced no visible symptom at this duration. Real finding: this system appears to have real resilience to brief redis unavailability, likely fail-open or retry/connection-pool-queueing behavior on the idempotency-check and payment-status-lookup code paths that depend on it. No conclusion possible from this evidence -- correctly cannot form a hypothesis, so this is being marked evidence-free rather than guessed.
blind_conclusion: ABSTAIN -- no detectable evidence anywhere in the window
confirmation_basis: Not applicable -- there is no evidence to confirm against. Recorded honestly as a real, informative null result: this fault type as currently parameterized (20s outage) is evidence-free on this system, analogous to the IDEMPOTENCY_COLLISION_STORM findings. Next step (not yet tested): try a longer outage duration to see if sustained Redis unavailability eventually produces visible degradation (TTL expiry, connection pool exhaustion under load) rather than being silently absorbed.
